descricao_original: When an arteriole leaves a trabecula and enters the parenchyma of the spleen, it is immediately surrounded by a sleeve of T-dependent, diffuse lymphatic tissue termed the periarterial lymphoid sheath, PALS. Because the arteriole is located near the center of the PALS, it is called the central arteriole. PALS forms one portion of the white pulp. 400x
creditos_identificados: Image source: Image taken of a slide from the University of Michigan collection.
